rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Only the first pair limits the score, and all compounds already elute before 10 minutes. Raise temperature while keeping the gradient unchanged to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity resolves that pair without adding a time penalty.

Lengthen the gradient one step to improve the first pair’s resolution from 1.41 toward full credit. The last peak at 6.56 minutes leaves ample room to reduce gradient steepness without incurring a time penalty.

The maximum CRF is reached; now test a shorter method by shifting the starting organic fraction upward while preserving injection 3’s gradient slope. This should advance elution, while checking whether the first pair retains sufficient resolution.

Use a slope between injections 2 and 3 while restoring the lower starting organic fraction that favored the critical first pair. This targets full resolution with earlier last-peak elution than injection 3.
Reduce the endpoint by one grid step to give the critical first pair slightly more separation. This should recover CRF 1.000 while keeping the last peak earlier than in injection 3.

Trim the endpoint and shorten the programmed gradient to 8 minutes, with a slope only slightly steeper than injection 6. The last peak should remain within the gradient, and the first pair may retain full resolution while elution becomes slightly faster.

Test a 6-minute gradient with a slope between injections 5 and 7, targeting first-pair resolution just above 1.5. The last compound may elute during the final hold, so this run checks whether trimming the endpoint preserves full resolution and rapid elution.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 4 while retaining its higher starting organic fraction, testing whether the first pair can regain full resolution. This probes an alternative fully resolved window; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

With maximum CRF already secured, explore a cooler, steeper gradient for a potentially faster fully resolved method. Temperature can reverse close-pair selectivity, so the low-temperature endpoint may offer a different resolution optimum.

Keep the low temperature and lengthen the gradient to determine whether the late three-peak cluster separates with reduced slope. The first pair is already resolved at this temperature, so this tests a distinct selectivity regime while likely keeping all peaks within 10 minutes.

The late cluster barely responds to gradient slope at 25 C, so increase temperature to shift its selectivity. An 8-minute gradient tests whether the first pair retains enough of its low-temperature separation while shortening elution relative to injection 11.

Raise temperature another step to separate the late cluster, using a shallower gradient to support resolution. The higher starting organic fraction tests whether a shifted window can preserve the low-temperature first-pair separation while offsetting some added retention time.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves first-pair selectivity in the cooler regime while shortening elution. The late cluster was resolved at 35 C, so this explores a faster alternative window with injection 8 retained as the best fast, fully resolved method.

Return to injection 13’s window start and reduce the gradient slope to improve its limiting first pair. This tests a lower-temperature maximum-score alternative, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Return to 60 C and test a higher starting fraction with a compensating shallower slope. This checks whether a further window shift can preserve first-pair resolution and accelerate the last peak; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

The higher starting fractions compromise the critical pair, so restore phi0 to 0.05 and use injection 3’s successful slope in a trimmed window. This targets a compact maximum-score method with more resolution margin than injection 8.

With the maximum score secured, test a slightly shallower trimmed gradient for greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test a slope of 0.0708 organic fraction per minute, between injections 4 and 9, to refine the resolution boundary at phi0 = 0.10. This should slightly shorten elution relative to injection 9 while potentially preserving full first-pair resolution.

Test a shallower version of injection 8 for greater resolution margin while targeting the same maximum CRF. Injection 18 suggests the first pair will improve and the third pair should remain resolved, with the last peak still below 10 minutes.

Lower the starting fraction relative to injection 15 while preserving its slope, aiming to lift the first pair above R = 1.5. This tests a fully resolved lower-temperature alternative, with last-peak elution estimated just below 10 minutes.

Reduce injection 15’s endpoint one step to raise its first-pair resolution above 1.5, while the higher starting fraction should keep the last peak below 10 minutes. This targets a maximum-score lower-temperature alternative; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Reduce injection 8’s endpoint one step to improve the critical first pair while retaining a 6-minute programmed gradient. The final hold will delay the last peak somewhat, but this tests a compact maximum-score method with more resolution margin.

Shift injection 23’s starting fraction upward while retaining its endpoint and duration, using the shallower slope to compensate for reduced early retention. This targets a shorter fully resolved alternative to injection 23, while injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Use a slope between fully resolved injections 9 and 24, with an endpoint high enough to avoid delaying the last peak during the hold. This targets maximum CRF with earlier elution than injection 24; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
